subject: Request: Pricing & Packaging review (dedicated sizing + usage forecast) - Pioneer Health

Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Pricing & Packaging review: Pioneer Health - dedicated capacity sizing

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the initial walkthrough last week. We've had a few internal follow-ups and there's alignment to move to a formal pricing/packaging review so our engineering, procurement, and security teams can sign off. Key asks from our side:

- Walk through recommended dedicated capacity / sizing based on our expected Q2 burst (attached is a simple usage snapshot).
- Understand cost vs. latency tradeoffs for quantized model variants.
- Confirm contractual SLAs and data handling for our PHI-adjacent workloads.

People we'd like on the call: myself, Rajiv (security), and someone from procurement (cc'd). We'd also love your SE to join to go over sizing.

Can you propose a 60-minute block next week? We are US-Eastern and prefer mornings.

Thanks,
Hannah

2) Ask list: can you share a 30-day token/hour peak estimate (or we can use the attached template if easier)?

Thanks for the sync, everyone — see attached a short pre-read that addresses the telemetry/audit questions and lays out sizing assumptions. High-level agenda for Tue 10:00–11:00 EST:

- 10:00–10:10: Introductions & goal alignment (Hannah / Rajiv)
- 10:10–10:25: Usage mapping & recommended dedicated profile (Mina)
- 10:25–10:40: Cost walk-through (Aditya / Grace)
- 10:40–10:50: Security/audit logs & key management (Mina + Rajiv Q&A)
- 10:50–11:00: Next steps / procurement path (Procurement rep + Grace)

A couple of notes on the sizing doc: we used the snapshot Hannah shared and filled the template with conservative burst estimates — the key variables are peak concurrent requests and average sequence length. If you have actual 7- or 30-day peak windows, send them before Tue and we can tighten the numbers.

Attachments included: capacity_sizing_notes.pdf (pdf), SLA_draft_redlines.pdf (pdf) — the SLA draft highlights exceptions that are typically negotiated for PHI-adjacent customers.

See you Tue. I'll plan to share a short model comparison (FP16 vs 8-bit quant) during the call.

— Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
